There are various reasons for this, but steps can definitely be taken to tackle this issue.  In my opinion, a main factor to blame for this issue is the problem ofpeople’s conception and selfishness. It is common for people tto get ha general conception of environmental protection, but they do not realize the seriousness of tpollution, which is mainly caused by their daily behaviors, such as driving private cars for freedom and convenience. Those exhaust fumes from vehicles lead to increasing global warming, which may have a devastating effect on the planet in the future. It is sometimes argued that companies should accept equal proportion of employees of each gender. However, I completely disagree with this point of view.  Having the same number of men and women in all enterprises is simply unrealistic. Employee numbers on any positions depend on the application that companies received. If a company decided to fill the job positionsv with equal numberof males and females, it would need enough applicants of each gender. However, in reality, many jobs are more popular with one gender than the other, and it would not be practical to aim for equal proportions for most of companies. For example, the construction area attracts more male applicants, and it would be difficult to fill these positions if fifty percent of places needed to go to females. All these extra physical steps slow down the news’ deliverying speed. When it comes to the news on the Internet, a simple click on editor’s keyboard would push the news to thousands and millions of devices in a quick secondi. Readers would certainly choose the Internet over newspapers for that they could be the first ones to be informed, instead of waiting for hours or days for their newspapers to appear in their mailbox.   Not only the newspapers are losing the speed battle to the Internet, they are having a challengingo time catering to the social nature of humans. While readers can quickly send the link to a piece of news to their friends using the Internet because they love sharing and communicating with each other, this is simply next to impossible with newspapers. For instance, I hardly see any of my friends would cut off a piece of newspaper and mail it to me just because they think the joke they saw on the newspaper would make me laugh, whereas I have received numerous memes from them in my email inbox on a daily basis. It is simply easier, faster and more economical to share news over the Internet and as humans, people love sharing.   In summary, I strongly believe that newspapers will soon die out as a media. question: The money spent by governments on space programs would be better spent on vital public services such as schools and hospitals. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay: In contemporary society, investing a large sum of money on space programs is favored by many countries. However, some people argue that the money should be used in public services rather than space missions. As for me, I agree with the claim from these peopleconsidering two major reasons.  First of all, it is uncertain whether the outcomes of the investment on space programs will be beneficial to the national economy or the opposite may happenAdmittedly, exploring the universe and exploiting the resources in outer space can provide the nation and the society with long-term profits, but the large expenditure will also become huge burdens for governments, thereby doing huge gharm to the economy in short term. For example, Soviet once invested considerable money on the space programs in order to compete with the U.S in the universe, which involved the government in endless financial problems, contributing to the fall of this superpower. Therefore, the large fortune sgiven to space missions may turn out to be disastrous to the economy and stability of the nation.  By comparison, expending more money on public service is bound to improve the public well-being, as the social equality may be achieved gradually with more ifacilities added. For instance, in many developing countries such as India and China, the shortage of educational resources causes unfair distribution in the society. Children in big cities receive education from qualified public schools, whereas those living in poverty-stricken areas can hardly afford to attend these institutions, thus causing great difference in learning standards among the youth. Such gap can even be wider when these young people step into job markets, twhereby increasing inequality in the society. Nevertheless, if the government spent more money on building standard schools in backwards lregions, this inequality can reduced to a large degree.  In conclusion, regarding the possible negative effects caused by huge expenditure on space missions as well as the positive transformation that may be supported by the money saved, I am in firm belief that more money should be given to those public service like building more schools than the space exploration or exploitation. (40’)

For consumerism, there has been almost unanimous consensus regarding the assumption that “‘ the newer the better, and that has led to impulsive consumption for newness.  For instance, the recent publish research result, that 80% of people are willing to purchase a mobile phone with newer versions regardless if  the new one has any advancement in the technology or how long they have been using the current one, manifests the impulsiveness of consumers. iIn order to convince consumers , retain their competitiveness and increase their sales revenue,  businesses will try to emphasize the newness of their products in their  promotion campaigns.    I believe whether the development is negative or positive mainly depends on if there is real innovation and novelty in the products.  If there are new elements  or further breakthroughs involved in the design as in the case of the Apple official press conferences, the advertising will bew informative and beneficial for consumers. By contrast, if the emphasis is an exaggeration of the products’ features, the promotion will be rather misleading and deceitful, leading to irrational consumption and impulsive purchases. In conclusion, the high demands of consumers for new products are ithe main underlying reasons of f the situation which, I believe, is not instinctively beneficial or harmful. For example, the number of police officers in the  population in China is less than 1% which is much less compared with the United States. However, the crime rate in China is much lower due to the mature and well-established security camera network. AI technologies enable the police to track down criminals through facle recognition and license plate recognition functions which are both cost-effective and labour-effective.  In my opinion, that giving longer prison terms to criminals can deter crime in some ways.
